## Introduction

In this post, I use both R and Python to explore the Palmer Penguins dataset. I will prepare the data in R and then use Python to summarize and visualize the results.

Data: [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/), Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

## Prepare the data in R

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)

penguins_r <- penguins |>
  select(species, body_mass_g) |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g))

penguins_r
```

## Analyze the R data with Python

```{python}
import pandas as pd

penguins_python = r.penguins_r

average_mass = (
    penguins_python
    .groupby("species", as_index=False)["body_mass_g"]
    .mean()
)

average_mass
```

## Visualize the result in Python

```{python}
#| label: fig-r-python-mass
#| fig-cap: "Average penguin body mass calculated from data prepared in R and visualized in Python."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.bar(
    average_mass["species"],
    average_mass["body_mass_g"]
)

plt.xlabel("Species")
plt.ylabel("Average body mass (g)")
plt.show()
```

## Findings

The data were first prepared in R and then passed to Python for further analysis. Python calculated the average body mass for each species and created the visualization. Gentoo penguins had the highest average body mass.
